claims.exact_statement: For the one-qubit channel E_(omega,tau)=exp(tau[-i omega[Z,.]+gamma(X(.)X-(.))]), fixed gamma>0 and tau>0, and every local operating point omega0 != 0, the exact finite-cycle channel has Choi rank 4 and Kraus-product span equal to all Hermitian qubit operators. Its local signal tangent is nonzero, so the optimal QFI over Q parallel or arbitrary sequential/adaptive channel uses with noiseless ancillas and parameter-independent controls is Theta(Q).
assumptions: One sensing-qubit channel use lasts exactly tau and the parameter-independent Markovian environment resets between uses.
gamma>0 and tau>0 are fixed as Q grows.
The signal Hamiltonian convention is H=omega Z, matching arXiv:2609.40022.
The local operating point is fixed at omega0 != 0; the parameter is locally estimable there.
Arbitrary ancillas, noiseless controls, recovery, and measurements are allowed between channel uses and are not charged.
claims.novelty_boundary: The asymptotic HNKS criterion and finite-rate QEC setting are established. This report reconstructs the full-rank finite-step mechanism for this transverse-noise channel and extends the exponent conclusion from specified CSS readouts to arbitrary channel strategies. Novelty and priority have not been externally checked.

costs.channel_uses: Q; one use costs tau sensing time, so sequential exposure is Q*tau.
costs.known_or_supplied: gamma, tau, and the local operating point omega0 are treated as calibrated inputs.
costs.controls: Noiseless ancillas, syndrome extraction, recovery, feedback, preparation, and measurement are free in the theorem-level comparison.
costs.coefficient: A finite O(Q) QFI coefficient is obtained by the channel-extension SDP; it was not numerically optimized here.
costs.excluded: Global/Bayesian risk, local-frequency acquisition, control energy, circuit depth, and temporally correlated environments.

claims.falsifier: At any fixed gamma,tau>0 and nonzero omega0, exhibit an exact zero Choi eigenvalue or a nonzero vector orthogonal to the trajectory Kraus span; alternatively exhibit an allowed adaptive strategy with QFI/Q unbounded as Q grows.
claims.next_gate: Write an explicit finite four-Kraus chart, compute the channel-extension SDP coefficient as omega0 approaches zero and tau approaches zero, and compare the result with prior finite-rate QEC papers.

claims.exact_statement: At the same fixed gamma>0,tau>0 but local point omega0=0, every quantum-jump trajectory is proportional to I or X, so S=span_H{I,X}; the trajectory-dilation signal component is H_mod_S=cZ with c=(1-exp(-2 gamma tau))/(2 gamma)>0. The local analytic Choi family admits a differentiable four-Kraus chart through the rank change. The HNKS theorem therefore gives optimal asymptotic QFI lim_(Q->infinity) F_Q(Q)/Q^2=4c^2 for arbitrary noiseless-ancilla parallel strategies, hence Theta(Q^2).
assumptions: Same finite-dimensional one-qubit Markovian channel as claim TRANSVERSE-QEC-FINITE-CYCLE-GENERIC-SQL.
The operating point is exactly omega0=0 and estimation is local at that point.

The analytic one-parameter Choi matrix is factored using local analytic eigenvalue/eigenvector branches; nonnegative vanishing eigenvalue branches have even-order zeros and signed analytic square roots.
Arbitrary ancillas and ideal controls are available; their resource costs are not included.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_HNKS_application; pointwise rank-change use relies on differentiable fixed-length four-Kraus chart (nonminimal at resonance), a bridge not explicitly discussed in the source theorem and pending independent proof review; global_uniform_estimation_unresolved; priority_unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The HNKS theorem is established. The resonance rank drop and coefficient c are reconstructed for this channel; no claim is made that the pointwise QFI law gives a uniform minimax or Bayesian advantage over an interval containing nonzero detunings.

costs.asymptotic_qfi_coefficient: 4c^2 per Q^2, with c=(1-exp(-2 gamma tau))/(2 gamma).
costs.unpriced: Growing-code/ancilla size, controls, recovery depth, state preparation, measurement, and operating-point acquisition.

claims.falsifier: Show the gauge-invariant Z component of i sum K_i^dagger partial_omega K_i at zero is not cZ modulo S, or show a smooth local Kraus chart cannot be formed for the analytic Choi family.
claims.next_gate: Construct and publish the explicit smooth four-Kraus chart and analyze the global risk when the prior has nonzero width around resonance.
claims.limitations: The imported theorem is pointwise in the operating parameter and stated in rank-r notation. An analytic Choi factorization gives a differentiable fixed-length chart through the rank change, so we judge the theorem applicable there; the source does not separately formulate a variable-minimal-rank corollary, and the chart bridge has not been externally proof-reviewed.

claims.exact_statement: The v1 preprint arXiv:2609.40022 (submitted 2026-09-30) studies CSS-code sensing with H=omega sum_i Z_i, independent transverse L_i=sqrt(gamma)X_i, logical-plus initialization, binary X-stabilizer projection, and ideal instantaneous recovery at fixed interval tau. It reports a finite Heisenberg-like sensitivity window and eventual SQL-like crossover for the Steane and Shor examples; for small tau its decay rates imply crossover time of order (gamma^2 tau)^(-1) for those fixed codes and readout.
assumptions: The preprint's code-specific signal/noise model and binary stabilizer measurement.
Instantaneous noiseless recovery every tau and fixed finite code size.
Local frequency operating point and independent repetitions as specified in the paper.
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite-rate QEC and finite windows were already studied in primary literature, including Shettell et al. 2021. This package does not claim priority for the finite-window observation.

costs.paper_model: Finite CSS code with specified binary readout; ideal recovery time and control energy are not charged.
costs.external_validation: No independent source-proof review or hardware replication performed.

claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the cited preprint equations and the stated fixed-code sensitivity envelope or small-tau decay rates.
claims.next_gate: Compare the finite-step channel-rank result and resonance exception with the full prior literature on discrete-time recovery, not only the papers cited by arXiv:2609.40022.
claims.currentness_as_of: 2026-10-08: live arXiv record still listed only v1 submitted 2026-09-30, with no journal reference.

claims.exact_statement: Using an 80-decimal-digit mpmath matrix exponential for the specified one-qubit Liouvillian at gamma=tau=0.1, the normalized Choi eigenvalues at omega=3 and omega=0.1 are strictly positive numerically, while at omega=0 two eigenvalues are zero to numerical precision.
assumptions: The Liouvillian and column-vectorization convention implemented in finite_channel_check.py.
Numerical eigensolve and finite precision are diagnostic, not proof.
claims.novelty_boundary: Checks three parameter points only and does not establish the all-parameter trajectory-span theorem.

costs.runtime: Small 4x4 matrix exponential plus 8x8 real symmetric eigensolve.
costs.precision: 80 decimal digits; inputs gamma,tau are parsed from decimal strings.

claims.falsifier: Reproduce the calculation with the stated model and find a non-positive eigenvalue away from omega=0 beyond numerical error, or nonzero rank-four eigenvalues at omega=0 beyond numerical error.
claims.next_gate: Use analytic Choi eigenvalues or the exact trajectory proof for global rank claims; retain this only as a smoke check.
